To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

artificial miRNAs and siRNAs can efficiently suppress HIV-1 mutants with one or two nucleotides mutations in the target site, and that the 3′-untranslated region of HIV-1 RNA is a good target site for artificial miRNAs.

(i) shRNAs and miRNA can inhibit HIV-1 mutants with one or two base mutations in the target site; (ii) the 3′UTR of the HIV-2 genome is more resistant to mutation than the 3′-UTR of the human immunodeficiency type 1 (iii) miRNAs can be used for inhibition of HIV-2 and other viruses with imperfect target sequences.

1) shRNAs and miRNA can inhibit HIV-1 variants that contain one or two mutations within the target sequence, 2) the knockdown efficiency depends on the location of the target sequence within the HIV-1 genome and 3) miRNA are more potent than shRNAs for inhibition of imperfect targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of RNAi as a new therapeutic approach to combat HIV-1.
the development of RNAi as an antiviral strategy against HIV-1 and related viruses.
the use of artificial miRNAs and siRNAs as antiviral agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs and siRNAs have a different mode of action. siRNAs induce target mRNA degradation, whereas miRNAs induce translational repression.
the use of miRNA and shRNA to target HIV-1 RNA is a promising approach to develop new antiviral therapies.
miRNA and shRNA can efficiently inhibit wild-type and escape variants of HIV-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the HIV-1 genome contains several potential miRNA targets in the 5′ UTR and 3′ UTL.
miRNAs are more potent in inhibiting HIV-1 variants than shRNAs.
miRNAs are more potent in targeting imperfect sequences than shRNAs, but shRNAs are more efficient in targeting viral RNA than miRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNAi-mediated inhibition can be achieved by targeting partially complementary target sequences in the 3’ UTR of viral RNA.
RNAi can be used to target imperfect sequences.
RNAi can inhibit viruses that have escaped from inhibition by targeting the 3′-untranslated region (UTR).
